The dampness-returning weather phenomenon of “Huinantian” generally appears in South China in February and March every year, mainly because after the cold air leaves, warm and humid air currents quickly counterattack, causing the temperature to rise and the air humidity to increase, and water droplets are easily produced on the surfaces of some cold objects after they encounter warm and humid air currents. The following table is “Some weather data for Jiangmen City in March 2012”:

<image1>

According to the data in the table, on which day was Jiangmen City most likely to have the “Huinantian” weather phenomenon in March 2012?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The dampness-returning weather phenomenon of “Huinantian” generally appears in South China in February and March every year, mainly because after the cold air leaves, warm and humid air currents quickly counterattack, causing the temperature to rise and the air humidity to increase, and water droplets are easily produced on the surfaces of some cold objects after they encounter warm and humid air currents. The following table is “Some weather data for Jiangmen City in March 2012”: <image1> According to the data in the table, on which day was Jiangmen City most likely to have the “Huinantian” weather phenomenon in March 2012?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
In the image there is a table titled “Some meteorological data for Jiangmen City in March 2012”; the date columns are the 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th, and 17th; the row items include weather conditions, average temperature (℃), and relative humidity (%). The table shows: from the 12th to the 14th the weather was all light rain, the average temperatures were respectively 14.5℃, 16.4℃, and 19.4℃, and the relative humidity was respectively 64—89%, 90—92%, and 73—86%; on the 15th the weather was sunny, the average temperature was 25.3℃, and the relative humidity was 81—89%; on the 16th and 17th it was cloudy, the average temperatures were respectively 19.5℃ and 18.9℃, and the relative humidity was respectively 57—86% and 48—66%.
According to the meaning of the question, “Huinantian” usually appears after cold air leaves and warm and humid air currents quickly counterattack, showing a clear rise in temperature and relatively high air humidity. Comparing day by day, it can be seen that from the 14th to the 15th the average temperature rose from 19.4℃ to 25.3℃, the largest increase, and the relative humidity on the 15th still reached 81—89%; at the same time, the weather changed from continuous light rain to sunny, matching the characteristics of warm and humid air currents counterattacking after cold air, temperature rising, and humidity being relatively high. Therefore, the date most likely to have “Huinantian” is the 15th.
